subject: Realtime output pauses observed during high-throughput demo — exec remediation path
summary: Customer reported reproducible ~3–7s pauses in streaming output during demo traffic peaks. Initial triage shows proxy queueing spikes and elevated kernel retransmits; customer asked for executive-visible remediation and a temporary SLA concession. Internal ask: confirm immediate mitigation (fallback to polling or enable chunked keepalive), gather traces + pcap, and prepare an exec-facing incident note and next-steps document.
messages:
From: Chris Holt <chris.holt@skylinehealth.com>
To: support@redwood.com, sean.gallagher@redwood.com
Cc: Alyssa Greene <alyssa.greene@skylinehealth.com>, sre@skylinehealth.com
Date: 2026-12-05T09:12:00Z
Subject: Realtime demo — intermittent output pauses (observed today)

Hi Sean / Redwood support team,

During our morning demo run at ~08:45 PT we saw the assistant stop emitting tokens for 3–7s several times while the client reported the WS connection stayed open. The UI shows the spinner but no bytes arrive for that window; then the stream resumes. This happened consistently when we ran 80 concurrent sessions (our expected peak). Attached is a Grafana snapshot and a client trace we captured.

This behavior killed the demo flow with our execs — they want an explanation and a plan. Can you confirm whether this looks like your side (chunk buffering / proxy) or a client-side retransmit issue?

Chris
Customer Success / Skyline Health
[attachment: skyline_grafana_snapshot.png (image/png)]
[attachment: client_trace_20261205.log (text/plain)]

From: sean_gallagher@redwood.com
To: Chris Holt <chris.holt@skylinehealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-05T09:28:00Z
Subject: Re: Realtime demo — intermittent output pauses (observed today)

Thanks Chris — sorry you hit this during a demo. We're treating this as a high-priority incident. Initial notes:

- Pattern (from your trace) looks like token-stream gaps with the TCP connection still established — that matches a chunked-transfer buffer pause rather than an early socket close.
- Possible sources: upstream proxy queueing under burst, server-side batching backpressure, or an intermittent kernel-level NIC interrupt coalescing spike we saw in a different case last quarter.

Immediate next steps we will take (now):
1) Dev team will pull server-side request traces and proxy queue metrics — request id(s) from your trace: rwd-req-6f2b6.
2) We will enable aggressive chunked keepalive and a shorter proxy buffer flush threshold for your account for the next 4 hours to see if it prevents pauses (non-disruptive).
3) If that doesn't help, we'll toggle a fallback to the non-streaming poll path for your demo traffic to preserve UX for execs.

Marissa / Dev / Kimberly — can you take ownership of 1–2 above? I flagged this for exec visibility (Kimberly) because Skyline has a renewal review next week.

Sean
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-05T09:42:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Realtime demo — intermittent output pauses (observed today)

Forwarding Chris' trace to Dev.

Dev — initial triage notes from ops: when we ran a replay against the staging pool we reproduced 4/10 runs with ~4s pause; the proxy_queue_length histogram shows spikes from 12 -> 180ms at ~50–70 qps bursts. Attached is the CSV extract.

Action I can take now: enable the keepalive/flush change Sean proposed on the Skyline ingress rule (10:50 PT). If that reduces pause frequency, we consider that a short-term mitigation. If not, we schedule the polling fallback and coordinate the customer UX doc.

Marissa
Incident Lead

From: dev_patel@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-05T10:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Realtime demo — intermittent output pauses (observed today)

Triage update — reproduced in staging with synthetic client at 70 concurrent slow-consumers. Root-cause hypothesis: under high concurrency our proxy coalesces chunked writes and then hits a backpressure window when the downstream socket is not reading (slow client). There is also a correlated increase in socket retransmits on the host (seen in tcp_retransmits counter), likely due to NIC interrupt coalescing and a kernel driver scheduling jitter.

What I will do now:
- Push a config change to Skyline's traffic class to reduce proxy write coalescing from 50ms -> 8ms and shorten flush threshold.
- Temporarily bump the per-connection write buffer so small pauses don't aggregate.
- Collect pcap for the failing replay (will attach).

If we still see pauses after these changes, next step is to opt the Skyline demo route into the polling fallback (no streaming) and prepare rollback instructions.

Dev
SRE / Runtime

From: sean_gallagher@redwood.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com, Chris Holt <chris.holt@skylinehealth.com>
Date: 2026-12-05T13:15:00Z
Subject: Exec note: ask for short-term concession + remediation plan

Kimberly — Skyline is asking for an exec-facing explanation and a remediation plan; the renewal review is Wednesday. Quick ask: can we authorize a one-time SLA concession (service credit) if the keepalive/flush change does not entirely eliminate disruption? They are a strategic account and the demo involved execs.

Proposed note to customer (short):
- Acknowledgement: we saw intermittent pauses during high-concurrency demo runs.
- Action taken: we applied aggressive chunked keepalive + reduced proxy coalescing; we collected traces and will monitor for 4 hours.
- Next step: if pauses persist, we'll enable a polling fallback for their demo and issue a goodwill credit while a deeper fix (kernel driver tuning + proxy rewrite) is scheduled.

Can you reply with approval to a concession or a different ask? If approved, I will send the exec-facing message and cc legal for formal credit terms.

Sean

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com
Cc: Chris Holt <chris.holt@skylinehealth.com>
Date: 2026-12-05T16:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Exec note: ask for short-term concession + remediation plan

Sean / team — thanks for the rapid triage and clear plan. Approve a goodwill credit up to 7% of the monthly committed spend if the mitigation does not fully resolve customer impact. Please do the following before sending the exec note to Skyline:

1) Capture a short (1-page) incident summary with timeline + mitigations (Marissa).
2) Attach collected traces (Dev) and a Grafana link to the monitored window.
3) Iterate the customer-facing note to include the concession language and an ETA for the deeper fix (targeting kernel tuning + proxy config release in the 2-week sprint).

Chris — appreciative of your patience. We will send the exec note within the hour and monitor the environment closely. If you see another pause please reply with the precise timestamp and we'll pull the matched request id.

Kimberly Park
VP, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
[Sent on behalf of Redwood leadership]
